Create Firewall Rules

You can use this page to create Firewall rules to block or allow specific traffic used by certain applications, such as video conferencing or some online games, through your Sky Hub.

Note: This feature is for Advanced Users only. Incorrect configuration may cause connection problems. Please check all configuration changes in the service or game user manual before applying.

IPv6 firewall rule

Enable IPv6 Firewall: This option will enable/disable only the user-defined Outbound and Inbound IPv6 firewall rules in the router.

Outbound Services

This lists all existing rules for outbound traffic. If you have not defined any rules, only the default rule will be listed. The default rule allows all outgoing traffic.

To create a new rule:

  • Select Add (it doesn't matter which radio button is selected).
  • The Outbound Service screen will be displayed.
  • Complete the Outbound Service screen, and save the data. The new rule will be listed in the table when you return to this screen.

To edit an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Edit to edit the selected rule.

To delete an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Delete to delete the selected rule.

To move up an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Up to move up the selected rule.

To move down an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Down to move down the selected rule.

Inbound Services

Enable Inbound IPv6 IPSec Firewall:
This option will enable/disable only the IPsec related inbound IPv6 firewall rules in router. It is independent of the Enable IPv6 Firewall option. Enabling this option allows devices to use IPv6 natively to improve connectivity to services like the Xbox One.

Allow Inbound ICMPv6 Echo Requests:
This option will allow/disallow ICMPv6 inbound echo requests to LAN hosts.

Inbound Services Table:
This lists all existing rules for inbound traffic. If you have not defined any rules, only the default rule will be listed. The default rule blocks all inbound traffic.

To create a new rule:

  • Select Add (it does not matter which radio button is selected).
  • The Inbound Service screen will be displayed.
  • Complete the Inbound Service screen, and save the data. The new rule will be listed in the table when you return to this screen.

To edit an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Edit to edit the selected rule.

To delete an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Delete to delete the selected rule.

To move up an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Up to move up the selected rule.

To move down an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Down to move down the selected rule.

It is not possible to configure IPv4 inbound firewall rules in carrier grade network connections.

Inbound Services

It is not possible to configure the inbound firewall rules for IPv4 Port Forwarding due to a feature enabled on your Sky Broadband connection.

If you wish to set up an inbound firewall rule please contact Sky Technical Support.

To create a new rule:

  • Select Add (it does not matter which radio button is selected).
  • The Inbound Service screen will be displayed.
  • Complete the Inbound Service screen, and save the data. The new rule will be listed in the table when you return to this screen.

To edit an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Edit to edit the selected rule.

To delete an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Delete to delete the selected rule.

To move up an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Up to move up the selected rule.

To move down an existing rule:

  • Tick the radio button next to a row in the table.
  • Select Move Down to move down the selected rule.
